law_name: NYC Local Law - Pistol Permit Restrictions
description: NYC continues strict pistol licensing; only NYPD-validated licenses valid within city limits
Required new semi-automatic pistols sold in NY to use microstamping technology to trace shell casings to firearms
NYC required recordkeeping of handgun ammunition sales to licensed dealers
Expanded NYPD-run gun buyback events citywide to remove illegal firearms from streets

First post-Sandy Hook gun law in the nation: universal background checks on all sales incl. private; assault weapons ban; 10-round magazine limit; mandatory mental health reporting; registration of grandfathered assault weapons; increased penalties for gun crimes
NYC implemented SAFE Act provisions including assault rifle registration; enhanced background check protocols at city level

law_name: NY SAFE Act - Ammunition Background Checks
description: Required background checks for all ammunition purchases (later repealed in 2015 due to database issues)
Repealed the ammunition background check provision of the SAFE Act due to implementation challenges with the federal database
Extreme Risk Protection Orders (ERPO): allows law enforcement and family members to petition courts to temporarily remove firearms from individuals posing a danger to self or others
Instituted a 30-day waiting period for firearm purchasers who do not pass an instant background check
Banned untraceable/unserialized ghost guns within NYC; required serialization of home-assembled firearms
Banned bump stocks and similar rate-of-fire enhancing devices statewide

10-bill package signed after Buffalo Tops shooting: strengthened red flag law; required safe storage; restricted large-capacity magazines; banned sale of body armor to civilians; required background checks on all semi-auto rifles; raised purchase age to 21 for semi-auto rifles; mandated reporting of lost/stolen guns

Enacted in response to SCOTUS Bruen ruling: requires 16 hrs classroom training + 2 hrs live range + written test for carry license; established extensive list of sensitive locations where carry is prohibited; required applicants to disclose social media accounts
NYPD began enforcement of CCIA sensitive location provisions across all five boroughs; most of NYC effectively designated as sensitive location
First-in-nation law allowing lawsuits against gun manufacturers and dealers for negligent business practices contributing to gun violence
Required financial institutions to use a special merchant category code for firearms and ammunition retailers to help detect suspicious bulk purchasing
Expanded economic support access for survivors and families of gun violence victims; broadened eligibility criteria
Required courts to notify statewide registry of protection orders when ERPOs are issued; effective February 2025

Six bills signed by Gov. Hochul including: ban on devices convertible to machine guns (auto sears); standardized mass shooting incident response protocols; additional ERPO improvements; school anti-violence education programs (signed Nov 2024)
NYPD adopted emergency rule allowing non-residents to apply for NYC Pistol License (NYPL) for the first time
Broadened legal definition of rape in NY law; noted here as it affected crime statistics reporting in NYC (increased reported rape incidents)
Strengthened ERPO notification law took effect; courts must notify statewide registry when temporary/final ERPOs are issued; over 14000 ERPOs ordered through Feb 2025

Signed legislation: banned sale of weapons convertible to machine guns; centralized gun violence prevention efforts; standardized mass shooting response; merchant category code expansion; 53% decline in shootings cited

law_name: Office of Gun Violence Prevention Codified
description: NY Office of Gun Violence Prevention permanently codified in state law through FY26 budget; $370M in gun violence prevention initiatives
